patterns.hint: Express route paths cannot contain '?'. Register the route without the query string (e.g. app.get('/search', ...)) and read the parameter inside the handler with req.query.paramName.
A value is undefined when you try to access a property on it. Add a guard before use, e.g.: if (!req.query.q) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'q is required' });
Variable '$1' was declared twice with const in the same scope. Every const must have a unique name.

Assertion got an empty array but expected data. Most likely cause: the data was deleted or never created before this line. Check whether a DELETE or clear-all step runs before this assertion and move the assertion earlier if needed.

patterns.hint: Deep-equal assertion failed. Verify that your expected object includes ALL fields the server returns, including null fields (e.g. author: null). Read the server handler to confirm the exact response shape.
The require path '$1' is wrong. server.test.js and server.js are in the same directory — use require('./server') (no .js extension, no ../ prefix).
npm package '$1' is not installed. Run: npm install $1

server.js is not exporting the Express app correctly. The file must end with `module.exports = app;` — not `module.exports = server` or the result of app.listen(). Also start the server only conditionally: `if (require.main === module) { app.listen(port, cb); }` so tests can import app without starting a server.

server.js started a listening server when it was require()d by the test. The server must only start conditionally: `if (require.main === module) { app.listen(port, cb); }` and must export `module.exports = app;`. Tests start their own server on port 0.

The test command hung and was killed. Most likely cause: the test file called app.listen() or a server.listen() at the top level outside any test() block, keeping the process alive forever. Move all server startup inside a test() block: const server = await new Promise(resolve => { const s = app.listen(0, () => resolve(s)); }); and always call t.after(() => server.close()) to clean up.

The test is trying to connect to port $1 but nothing is listening there. Tests must start the server themselves on port 0 and use the assigned port: const server = await new Promise(resolve => { const s = app.listen(0, () => resolve(s)); }); const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`; Do not hardcode any port number. Do not call API helpers outside a test() block.
Port already in use. In tests, pass port 0 to listen so the OS picks a free port: app.listen(0, cb) and read the actual port from server.address().port.

Syntax error: $1. Use write_file to rewrite the entire file correctly from scratch — do NOT use replace_text, which can introduce bracket mismatches. Read the file first, fix the error mentally, then write the complete corrected file.
